prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Episodes and intervals'. A long horizontal ribbon of unnumbered calendar tiles, softly perspective-painted. Toward the left a short cluster of coral tiles under a simple geometric VIRUS SYMBOL and a tissue box; a curved sound-ripple symbol beside them; label 'Viral infection + wheeze'. Then a longer clear ivory and teal stretch with small play blocks, labelled 'Well between episodes'. Toward the right a second separate coral cluster with the same simple virus symbol, tissue box and sound ripple; again label 'Viral infection + wheeze'. Gentle time arrow below, no dates or day numbers. Main takeaway 'Ask about interval symptoms'. Bottom qualifier 'Illustrative pattern, not a diagnosis'. Virus symbols are abstract badges, not electron microscopy. Absolutely NO clouds, rain, snow, weather, cold-temperature symbol or chilly blue child. No lungs, airways, inhaler technique or clinical chest sounds recording.

clinicalSources.title: Royal United Hospitals Bath: Preschool wheeze

teaching.question: Why ask how a preschool child breathes between wheezing illnesses?
teaching.answer: A common pattern is viral-triggered wheeze with well intervals. Symptoms between infections help characterise the illness and guide assessment; the episodic pattern alone does not exclude asthma.

title: Episodes and the intervals between them
caption: In a common preschool wheeze pattern, viral infections trigger episodes and the child is well between infections. The interval history matters; this pattern alone does not rule out asthma.
alt: An unnumbered calendar ribbon shows two viral-infection-and-wheeze clusters with virus badges, separated by a clear well interval.
